Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:99: The third: to be present in the synagogue, whether for prayer or for occupying oneself with Torah, if possible, for whoever comes to the synagogue is called a fearer of the Lord, as it is said (Isaiah 50:10) "who among you fears the Lord, who heeds the voice of His servant, who walks in darkness and has no light?" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in Tractate Berachot (6b) that this is said of one who is accustomed to come to the synagogue and one day did not come - their words: Ravin bar Rav Adda said in the name of Rav Chisda, whoever is accustomed to come to the synagogue and one day does not come, the Holy One, blessed be He, inquires after him, as it is said, "who among you fears the Lord, who heeds the voice of His servant, who walks in darkness and has no light? Let him trust in the Name of the Lord and rely upon his God" - if he went for a matter of mitzvah, he has "no light" [meaning: temporarily, but is otherwise fine]; if for an optional matter, he has no light. What is the reason? He should have trusted in the Name of the Lord, but did not trust. And in the Zohar, portion of Balak (196a), there is a sweet matter in the explanation of this verse - examine it there, for it is relevant to our discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:100: The reason one who comes to the synagogue is called a fearer of the Lord is that the synagogue is a small sanctuary, of which it is said (Leviticus 19:30) "and you shall fear My sanctuary"; and further, the place of fear stemming from judgment is in the synagogue, for there a fire of brightness rests upon the heads of Israel, as we shall elaborate in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:101: The fourth: to draw close to everyone who fears the Lord, and to distance oneself from one who does not fear the Lord, even from speaking with him in the manner of companionship. This is learned from what David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:63) "I am a companion to all who fear You," etc. The reason is that in drawing close to the good, he learns from their deeds, and further, the Shechinah, called "fear," is with them, and the light of the Shechinah shines upon him; and the opposite, "but a companion of fools shall be broken" (Proverbs 13:20). This is learned from what our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Yoma 9b), that whoever conversed with Reish Lakish, people trusted him without a deed and without witnesses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:102: The fifth: it is written (Psalms 34:12-14) "come, children, listen to me, I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the man who desires life," etc., "guard your tongue from evil," etc. It appears that the first levels a person ascends in fear are these: first, "guard your tongue from evil," etc.; second, "turn away from evil and do good"; third, "seek peace," etc. - and we elaborated on the explanation of these verses in the Gate of Holiness, chapters 10 and 11. The second, "turn away from evil," also pertains to fear, and we explained its matter in chapter 4 of this Gate; "seek peace" pertains to the matter of "and do good," and we explained it there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:103: The sixth: the prophet Isaiah, peace be upon him, explains this by saying (Isaiah 29:13) "and their fear of Me is a commandment of men, learned by rote." It appears that a person must inquire and know in truth whom he serves and whom he fears, along the lines of what David, peace be upon him, commanded Solomon, peace be upon him (I Chronicles 28:9) "know the God of your father and serve Him." The reason is that one who serves in the manner of a commandment of men learned by rote sometimes does and sometimes does not, and his heart is not fixed in faith, and if a gentile or someone like him comes and refutes his faith with proofs and difficulties, he may be defeated; but one who serves with knowledge in his heart is never defeated in any way. The punishment for serving as a commandment of men learned by rote is explained by the prophet afterward, saying (Isaiah 29:14) "therefore, behold, I will again do a marvelous work among this people, a marvelous and wonderful work, and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hidden" - since it is measure for measure: since they did not wish to become wise in Torah, to know the matter of the fear of the Creator in truth, so wisdom shall perish from the wise.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:104: Along these lines, since the place of fear is Yud, as explained in chapter 2 of this Gate, one must become wise in fear, and it should not be a commandment of men learned by rote; and therefore it says (Avot 2:5) "an ignoramus cannot fear sin," and if not, God forbid, the wisdom that is the source of fear becomes hidden.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:105: So too, this punishment relates back to what is said at the beginning of the verse: "because this people draws near with its mouth and honors Me with its lips, but has removed its heart far from Me, and their fear of Me," etc. - since he speaks with his God without the understanding of his heart being with him, his punishment is that the understanding of his prudent men becomes hidden; with this the whole verse is precise, without any superfluity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:106: Along these lines, one must also be careful in the recitation of his prayer and blessings, that they be with concentration and not a commandment of men learned by rote, as it says (Isaiah 29:13) "with his mouth and with his lips he honors Me, but his heart is far from Me," etc. And they say in Sefer Chasidim (siman 46): a story is told of a man who died several years before his time; many years later he appeared in a dream to one of his relatives, who asked him, "how do you fare in the world where you are?" He said to him, "every day I am judged for not having been precise in the blessing over bread, and the blessing over fruits, and the Grace after Meals, with concentration of heart, and they say to me, you intended it for your own benefit." He asked him, "but is the judgment of Israel's wicked not [limited to] twelve months, and more than that has already passed for you, yet they still judge you?" He said to him, "they do not judge me with punishments as severe as in the first twelve months" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:107: Among the merits of fear, in the World to Come, is "how great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You" (Psalms 31:20), and in this world, being watched over by an open eye, the eye of Arich Anpin, as it is written (ibid. 33:18) "behold, the eye of the Lord is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness"; (ibid. 103:11) "for as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His kindness toward those who fear Him"; and likewise (ibid. 103:13) "as a father has compassion on his children, so the Lord has compassion on those who fear Him." The reason is that the God-fearing person causes the subduing of the powers of judgment, as David the king, peace be upon him, explained, and therefore it is fitting that mercy be drawn upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:108: Among its merits is what is mentioned in the psalm (Psalms 112:2) "happy is the man who fears the Lord, who delights greatly in His commandments; his seed shall be mighty in the land," etc. Among its merits is that fear causes an increase in life, as it is written (Proverbs 10:27) "the fear of the Lord adds days"; and so they say in Midrash Pesikta (DeRav Kahana, siman 27), on the verse (Psalms 16:11) "You shall make known to me the path of life, fullness of joy in Your presence" - Rabbi Yudan said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, "make known to me the path of life"; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "David, do you seek life? Look to fear, as it is said, the fear of the Lord adds days" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:109: With this the chapter is concluded, and this Gate is concluded - blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:1: In explaining the necessity that service be with love, and the essence of the matter of love, as found in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, and in the books of the earlier pious ones.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:2: That our service should be with love, we were commanded in the Torah, in Deuteronomy, several times - whether in the portion "and now, Israel," as we have written above, or in the portion of Shema (Deuteronomy 6:5) "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart," or in the portion "and it shall come to pass, if you hearken" (ibid. 11:13) "to love the Lord your God and to serve Him." And Rabbeinu Moshe of Coucy writes in Sefer Mitzvot HaGadol, concerning the commandment to love - his words: "and because this passage is beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is the key to our fear, containing the unity of the Creator and the warning to love His Name with all the heart, all the soul, and all the might, and the whole Torah is contained within it - for whoever loves the King, all his thoughts are to do what is good and right in his eyes - therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded that we make five remembrances of it every day: (1) to read this passage when lying down, (2) and when rising, (3) that this passage be written opposite your heart, in the tefillin of the left arm, positioned opposite the heart, as it is said (ibid. 11:18) 'and you shall place these My words upon your heart,' and our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded that its placement should be opposite the heart; (4) that this passage be written opposite your soul, that the head-tefillin be placed upon the brain, which is precisely aligned with the space between the eyes above, since the essence of the soul and the settling of a person's mind is there, and this is 'and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes' (ibid. 6:8); (5) that this passage be written opposite your might, on the mezuzot of your house and your gates, since a person's wealth is there. And in the order they are written in Scripture - heart first, then soul, then wealth - so were they commanded in this order: 'and you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand,' opposite your heart; 'and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes,' opposite your soul; 'and you shall write them upon the mezuzot of your house and your gates,' opposite your might" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:3: When you examine these five occasions mentioned, they total ten, since the passage "and it shall come to pass, if you hearken" also mentions the matter of love, and it is [written] in the tefillin and mezuzah, and we recite it when lying down and when rising.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:4: Further, I found that the commandment to love is mentioned nine times in Deuteronomy: one, in the portion of Va'etchanan, in "and you shall love" (Deuteronomy 6:5). Four in the portion of Ekev, in the portion "and now, Israel" (ibid. 10:12), where it is said, "to walk in all His ways and to love Him"; (ibid. 11:1) "and you shall love the Lord your God, and keep His charge," etc.; (ibid. 11:13) "to love the Lord your God and to serve Him with all your heart," etc.; (ibid. 11:22) "for if you diligently keep all this commandment which I command you to do it, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to cleave to Him." Further, in the portion of Shoftim VeShotrim, it is mentioned once (ibid. 19:9) "to love the Lord your God and to walk in His ways all the days." And in the portion "Atem Nitzavim," three are mentioned (ibid. 30:6) "and the Lord your God will circumcise your heart," etc., "to love the Lord your God," etc.; (ibid. 30:16) "which I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments"; and at the end of the portion (ibid. 30:20) "to love the Lord your God, to heed His voice, and to cleave to Him" - this makes nine. And the commandment to love the convert, in the portion of Ekev (10:19), makes ten, corresponding to the ten sefirot - loving the convert corresponds to the tenth attribute, called Righteousness [Tzedek], and indeed the convert is called "righteous" [tzedek]. Thus the commandment of love is doubled and repeated many times, because it is the root of all divine service, and it is the ultimate perfection of the soul, that it cleave to its Maker, as it says, "to love," etc., "and to cleave to Him," as will be explained, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:5: Concerning the matter of love, our Sages, of blessed memory, say in the Sifrei - their words: "'and you shall love the Lord your God' - act from love, for there is a difference between one who acts from love and one who acts from fear: one who acts from love, his reward is doubled and redoubled, for it says, 'you shall fear the Lord your God' - you may have a person who fears his fellow; when the fellow burdens him, he leaves him and goes away, but you, act from love, for there is no love in the place of fear and fear in the place of love, except regarding the attribute of the Omnipresent alone" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:6: Further, in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 28): what is the difference between love and fear? They gave a parable: to what can this be compared? To a king who had two servants, one who loved the king and feared him, and one who feared him but did not love him. The king went to a country overseas; the one who loved the king and feared him arose and planted gardens and orchards and every kind of delicacy; the one who feared him and did not love him sat and did nothing. When the king came back from overseas, he saw gardens, orchards, and every kind of delicacy arranged before him, corresponding to the mind of the one who loved him; once the one who loved him came before the king and saw every kind of delicacy arranged before him, his mind was set at ease, corresponding to the king's joy. But the one who feared him and did not love him - once the king entered his house, all kinds of ruins were all arranged before him, corresponding to the mind of the one who feared; once the fearful one came before the king and saw all kinds of ruins arranged before him, his mind was shaken, corresponding to the king's wrath, as it is said (Psalms 111:5) "He has given food to those who fear Him" - this refers to this world. From this you learn that the reward of the one who loves is two portions, and the reward of the one who fears is one portion; therefore the wicked merit only this world, but there are those who shall eat of two worlds - this is what Scripture says (Song of Songs 8:7) "many waters," etc.; its ending I have quoted in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:7: What emerges for us from the totality of this passage is that the essence of love is that a person performs the King's desire in order to gladden Him, and even though he knows that from those very trees he plants, the King will give him varieties of delicacies as reward for what he planted, nevertheless the intent of the lover is only that the King's mind be set at ease by his joy, for the King is glad to see gardens, orchards, and trees planted before Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:8: The moral is understood: those who fear are the nations, idol worshipers, all of whom fear, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:7) "who would not fear You, King of the nations... for among all the wise men of the nations... there is none like You" - explained in the portion of Mishpatim (Zohar 95b-96a), that they all admit there is none like You, but they do not perform mitzvot; yet they are fearful. And those who love are Israel, who perform mitzvot, and in performing mitzvot and engaging in Torah is the planting of trees they plant above, supernal illuminations in which the King rejoices, since everything depends on the arousal from below, as I explained several times. And from the supernal light they drew down through performing mitzvot, their souls delight in the World to Come, along the lines of "whoever labors on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:9: In Nedarim (62a), it is taught: "to love the Lord and to cleave to Him" (Deuteronomy 30:20) - let a person not say, "I will read [Scripture] so that they call me wise," "I will study [Mishnah] so that they call me Rabbi," "I will study so that I will be called an elder and sit in the assembly"; rather, learn from love, and honor will come in the end, as it is said (Proverbs 7:3) "bind them upon your fingers, write them on the tablet of your heart," and it says (ibid. 3:17) "her ways are ways of pleasantness," and it says (ibid.) "she is a tree of life" - so far. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says: perform deeds for their own sake and speak of them for their own sake; do not make them a crown to be aggrandized with, nor a spade to dig with, etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:10: Further, they say in the midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, siman 871), on "who delights greatly in His commandments" - Rabbi Elazar said, in His commandments, and not in the reward of His commandments - and this is what we learn (Avot 1:3): Antigonus of Socho used to say, do not be like servants who serve their master in order to receive a reward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:11: Further, they say in the Sifrei (Ekev 5): "to love" - lest you say, "behold, I am learning Torah so that I may become rich, so that I may be called Rabbi, for the reward of the World to Come" - the verse teaches, "to love" - whatever you do, do only from love - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:12: In the Zohar, portion of Va'etchanan (267a), they say - their words, on the verse (Deuteronomy 6:5) "and you shall love the Lord your God": "'and you shall love' - a person must bind himself to Him in love, for whatever supernal service a person must perform for the Holy One, blessed be He, he should perform it in love, for there is no service like the love of the Holy One, blessed be He" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:13: In the Tikkunim (73b), it says that one who serves in order to receive a reward has a punishment - his words, briefly: "but love and fear apply both in good and in evil; and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, says (Song of Songs 2:7) 'I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love until it please' - this is love [given] and reward, until it pleases, and not in order to receive a reward. But fear and love in order to receive a reward - this is a maidservant, and 'under three things the earth trembles - under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress'" (Proverbs 30:23) - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:14: Concerning the matter of love, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes - his words, at the end of the Gate of Trust, and in the Gate of Love, and I have gathered his words briefly, focused on our purpose (Gate of the Love of God, chapter 1): the matter of love is the yearning of the soul and its inclination in itself toward the Creator, so that it may cleave to His supernal light. The soul is a spiritual essence that inclines toward things similar to it among spiritual beings, and by its nature distances itself from what is opposite it, the coarse bodies; and when the Creator bound it to this coarse body, which He wished to test it with by its governance of it, He aroused it to have compassion on it and to yearn for it, in order to seek rest from the illness of its body. And when the soul senses a matter that will add to it light in itself and strength in its soul, it will incline in its intent [thought] toward Him and cleave to Him in its thought and desire Him and yearn for Him - especially when a person knows the purpose intended in his creation and his coming forth into this perishable world, and recognizes the greatness of the other, enduring world, he will despise this world and its causes, and flee in his thought and his soul and his body to God, blessed be He, and delight in remembering Him in solitude, and be astonished at nothing but the thought of His greatness; and if he is among gatherings, he will desire nothing but His will, and yearn for nothing but to encounter Him, and his yearning for Him will be with effort, diligence, and alacrity - similar to what is said (Isaiah 26:9) "my soul yearns for You in the night," etc., and it says (ibid. 26:8) "for Your Name and for Your remembrance is the desire of the soul," and it says (Psalms 42:3) "my soul thirsts for God, for the living God," and it says (ibid. 63:2) "God, You are my God, I seek You early; my soul thirsts for You, my flesh yearns for You," etc. And then the soul will drink the potion of love in God and be alone in unifying its heart in Him, to love Him and trust in Him and yearn for Him, and have no occupation but the occupation of His service, and let nothing pass over its thoughts but Him, and let nothing arise in its thought but Him, and let it not send forth any of the limbs of its body except in what is drawn by it for His sake, and let it not loosen its tongue except in remembering His praise and His thanksgiving and His glorification, out of love for Him and yearning for His will, blessed be He; and if He does good to it, it gives thanks, and if He afflicts it, it bears it, and its body and soul and money are delivered to the sanctification of His Name, blessed be He, and it adds nothing to this but love for Him and trust in Him - as they said of one of the pious, who would rise at night and say, "my God, You have made me hungry and left me naked and made me dwell in the darkness of night, yet You have taught me Your might and Your greatness; if You burn me with fire I will add nothing but love for You and rejoice in You" - similar to what Job said (13:15) "though He slay me, yet I will hope in Him." And to this matter the Sage alluded when he said (Song of Songs 1:13) "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts" - and the Sages, of blessed memory, said, in the manner of exposition (Shabbat 88b), "even though he embitters me and makes me bitter, he shall lodge between my breasts." And similar to what they said (Berachot, chapter 9, mishnah 5), "and you shall love the Lord your God," etc. - "even if He takes your soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:15: The strongest of the things that help you toward this supreme level is great awe of God and dread of Him, and fear of His commandments, and constant thought of His watching over your secret and your open acts, your hidden and your visible, His governance of you and His compassion upon you, His knowledge, hidden and revealed, past and future, of your deeds and your thoughts, His goodness to you and His drawing you near - and you will not be able, in the face of all this, to keep from inclining toward Him in your heart and your innermost being with a pure heart and complete faith, and you will hang your soul upon love and trust in His compassion and the greatness of His graciousness and His mercy, and you will not, at that time, share with your love of Him any love of another, nor will it appear to you that you fear anything besides Him, nor will you neglect Him from your thoughts, nor will He depart from before your eyes, and your companionship will be in solitude, and He will sit with you in the wilderness, and a place full of people will be in your eyes as though empty, and empty of them as though not empty; you will not be desolate at their absence nor grieve at their loss, and you will always be joyful in God, glad in your Creator, rejoicing in His will, yearning to encounter Him, as it is written (Psalms 64:11) "the righteous shall rejoice in the Lord," and the prophet said (Habakkuk 3:18) "but I will rejoice in the Lord," and David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 27:1) "the Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?" and the rest of that psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:16: Close to these words, it is written in Sefer HaRokeach (Laws of Piety, root of the love of the Name) - his words: "the root of love is that the soul be full of the love of the Lord, bound with cords of love, with joy and gladness of heart, and not like one who serves his master against his will; rather, even if they were to protest against him, the love burns within him to serve and rejoice in fulfilling his Creator's will, as the Psalmist said (Psalms 100:2) 'serve the Lord with gladness,' and one who serves with uprightness of heart, and for the upright of heart there is joy (ibid. 97:11). And he does not serve for his own benefit or for his own honor, and he says, 'what am I, despised and a cessation of men, here today and tomorrow in the grave, formed in iniquity and full of filth - how was I chosen to be a servant of the King of Glory?' For when the soul thinks deeply about fear, the spark of the heart's love burns within it, and joy and the gladness of the innards increase, and gladness of heart and rejoicing of the kidneys grow great; a man's wisdom lights up his face, and those who love His Name rejoice in it, for every man in whose heart is the wisdom of the Name thinks with joy of the desire to do his Creator's will, to perform His commandments with his whole heart. And the lover does not think of the pleasure of this world and is not concerned with pleasure-trips with his wife nor with his sons and daughters, and all of it is as nothing before him - only to do his Creator's will and to bring merit to others and to sanctify His Name and to give himself over in love for Him, like Abraham (Genesis 14:23) 'I have raised my hand to the Lord... that I will not take so much as a thread or a shoelace,' and like Pinchas, who gave himself over when he killed Zimri. And they do not exalt themselves, and do not speak idle words, and do not look at women's faces, and hear their own disgrace and do not answer back, and all their thoughts are with their Creator, and they sweeten songs for their Master, and all the design of their thoughts burns with the fire of His love - happy is he in this world and the next" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:17: In Sefer Ta'amei HaMitzvot by Rabbi Yitzchak ibn Farchi, he writes concerning the reason for love, that when there is love within us, we cause the supernal cherubim to be unified face to face, and there is love between them, and He pours out good oil upon Malchut, and from there to Metatron and the holy Chayot, and the rest of the worlds are all filled with flow and blessing - so far, in brief, his intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:18: In the Zohar, portion of Va'etchanan (263b), they explain the matter of love - their words: "the commandment to love - we have already established that this is the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, which a person must love with great love, like Abraham, who feared the Holy One, blessed be He, with such great love that he gave over his body and soul to Him. From this we learn that whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the Ten Utterances, above and below, and therefore all those ten trials with which Abraham was tested, and he stood firm in all of them - all of them correspond to the Ten Utterances, every trial being an utterance, and he was tested with that utterance and stood firm in it, and therefore they are ten trials, and Abraham stood firm in all of them because he was bound and cleaved to the right hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is Ahavah Rabbah [Great Love]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:19: Why is it called Ahavah Rabbah? Because this love stands bound in the supernal world, "eternal love" [ahavat olam] - this is the secret of the lower world, without separation, in which His love is bound, and it is all a single secret. And it has been said, the secret of love: this love rises above all the services of the world; through this the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted more than everything and blessed - blessed is He forever and ever, and the secret of love is what is said" - so far. Here it is explained from this passage that the essence of love is to give over one's body and soul for the sanctification of the Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:20: This is likewise explained in the Tikkunim (10b) - their words: "'and the wise shall shine' - these are those who know a second secret in the commandments, in the word 'Bereishit,' which is Ahava [love], adding up in small [gematria] to one sum - and this is the love of Chesed, which is seventy-two in number, corresponding to the Name derived from the verses 'and it journeyed, and it came, and it stretched out' [Vayisa, Vayavo, Vayet], in which Vav counts as one - namely the utterance 'echad' [one], which is 'Bereishit,' concerning which it is established (Avot 5:1), 'could the world not have been created with a single utterance?' And this is the love of one's Master, whoever gives over his soul in unity, in love of his Master; and therefore (Deuteronomy 6:5) 'and you shall love the Lord your God' - even if He takes your soul - for if his soul is dearer to him than his body, therefore it says 'with all your soul'; and if his body is dearer to him than his money, therefore it says 'with all your heart'; and if his money is dearer to him than his body, therefore it says 'with all your might' - whatever is dear to you, give it over in love of your Master at a time of distress. This is the trial that Israel is destined to be tested with in the seventy years of the final exile, when a poor man is considered as dead, as though his soul were taken - body, soul, and money are all equal; whatever is dear to him, he gives it over in love of his Master, and at that time he is bound to the word Ahavah, which is Bereishit, as though the world were created through him. And whoever does not give over his soul and his body or his money in love of his Master at a time of distress is as though he returned the world to chaos and void, and therefore the verse follows it, 'and the earth was chaos and void'; and whoever gives over his body and his soul and his money in love of his Master is certainly, in that world, above no one."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:21: "And you shall love," etc. - this is Malchut, comprised of all the sefirot, and it is the commandment of the Holy One, blessed be He, within all six hundred and thirteen commandments, and concerning her it is said (Esther 3:3) "why do you transgress the king's commandment?" And she is the building of the world; the evil maidservant is the destruction of the world, and therefore it is said of her, "and the earth was chaos and void," and she is a strap in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, to lash the wicked with. And therefore whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, from his soul or his body or his money, the Holy One, blessed be He, protects - behold, his love is dependent on what is given to him, and this is not the essence of his love; this love, if his money or body is taken and he denies Him, is not the essence of love, until he gives over his soul in love of his Master, and if all three are equal to him, he gives them all over for the sanctification of His Name in love - this is the essence of love, which is the love of Malchut, which is the love of Chesed; fear is from the side of Gevurah - and from Chesed is Malchut, the love of Yud, as has been said; from Gevurah is the fear of the Lord; and the Torah, which is 611, is given to Israel from both of them, and this is the central pillar - from its side it is called Malchut, "the Torah of the Lord is perfect," and it is His commandment within all six hundred and thirteen commandments that depend on His Name, for they are Shin-Mem [365, negative commandments] together with Yud-Heh [equaling] 365, Zayin-Kaf-Reish-Yud [248, positive commandments] together with Vav-Heh [equaling] 248 - it is in His image, in His likeness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:22: To understand the words of these passages, which say that love is to give over one's soul and body for the sanctification of the Lord, we must quote the words of Rashbi concerning love (Bereishit 11b), where the root of love is explained - his words: "the second commandment: this is the commandment in which fear's commandment is unified, and does not depart from it forever, and it is love - for a person to love his Master with a complete love. And what is complete love? This is Ahavah Rabbah, as it is written (Genesis 17:1) 'walk before Me and be perfect' - complete in love. And this is what is written (ibid. 1:3) 'and God said, let there be light' - this is complete love, called Ahavah Rabbah; and here is the commandment for a person to love his Master as is fitting."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:23: Rabbi Elazar said: father, I have heard of this love in its completeness. He said to him: say it, my son, before Rabbi Pinchas, since he stands at this level. Rabbi Elazar said: Ahavah Rabbah is complete love, in the completeness of two sides, and if it is not comprised of two sides, it is not proper love in completeness; and therefore we learn that love, the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is divided into two sides. There is one who loves Him because he has wealth, length of days, sons around him, dominion over his enemies, his ways set right for him - and because of this he loves Him; but if this were reversed and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon him a turn of harsh judgment, it would become hateful to him and he would not love Him at all - therefore this love is not love that has an essential root. Love that is called complete is that which exists on both sides, both in judgment and in goodness, and the arrangement of his ways, that he loves his Master, as we learn, "even if He takes your soul from you" - this is complete love, existing on both sides; and therefore the light of the account of Creation went forth and was afterward hidden away - when it was hidden away, harsh judgment went forth, and the two sides were comprised together to become this completeness, proper love" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:24: Here it is explained, from this passage, that the essence of love is to comprise Chesed within the judgment of Gevurah - this is "with all your soul," to give over one's soul for the sanctification of the Name, that when the Holy One, blessed be He, tests him and bestows upon him any aspect of judgment, whether small or great, reaching even the giving over of his soul, out of his great love for the Holy One, blessed be He, he gives over his soul and body - such as Chananya, Mishael, and Azaryah into the fiery furnace, and many like them - here Chesed is comprised within judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:25: Likewise, one must comprise Gevurah within Chesed, for a person loves the Holy One, blessed be He, from the side of His kindnesses and the abundant flow of His goodness upon him, and this stems from the side of Chesed; then he should not trust in his good deeds, but rather fear judgment, and say, perhaps sin will be the cause, along the lines of Jacob, who said (Genesis 32:8) "and Jacob was greatly afraid," as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapters 3 and 5 - here we find Gevurah comprised within Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:26: This is complete love, that there is no completeness for Chesed except through comprising Gevurah within it, and no completeness for Gevurah except through comprising Chesed within it; and the secret is "YHVH, He is God, YHVH, He is God" (I Kings 18:39), as is explained (Zohar, Acharei 65a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:27: For this reason, the word "love" [ahavah] found first in the Torah is with Isaac, in the matter of the Binding (Genesis 22:2) "take now your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac" - meaning, to comprise Gevurah within Chesed, for "Abraham, My beloved" (Isaiah 41:8) refers to Chesed, since love unqualified is from the side of Chesed; "Isaac" is the Gevurah comprised within it. And so afterward it is mentioned (Genesis 24:67) "and she became his wife, and he loved her" - from the side of the Chesed comprised within him, for by the merit of the Binding, in which he subdued the judgment within himself and bound it beneath the Chesed that is Abraham, Chesed was comprised within him; therefore there is love within him, which is Chesed, to love Rivkah and bind her to himself - as we shall further elaborate on the secret of love in the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:28: We find, then, that the essence of love is, from the side of judgment, to give over one's soul for the sanctification of the Name; and since he is not concerned for his body, which was created according to nature in the Name Elohim, he then becomes sanctified in the love of Chesed, and Chesed overpowers judgment, since all the workings of the world are governed according to nature [teva], which is Elohim.
